answer: Picture each new agent as a sapling in an orchard: it can't vote or earn until a sponsor with proven history vouches for it and locks part of its own balance as collateral. If the sapling turns out to be a sybil, the sponsor loses that stake. An attacker can't conjure a lagoon of fake identities cheaply; each needs a real backer risking funds, so a farm of clones faces a frozen tundra of cost.
